title: The lookup revalidation prints current for a section-kept or unchanged fact only when the baseline is no newer than the fact's last confirmation, as apply does
goal: The lookup revalidation (factdiff.revalidate) prints current for a fact kept by its section, or for an unchanged or pinned source, only when the baseline is no newer than the anchor's last confirmation (verified_utc), as apply's kept() requires (otherwise the passage is resolved): a stubbed pack_revalidate case with verified_utc before detected_utc and the anchor's passage in neither text expects an outcome other than current.

gates.question: A pinned source with no stored baseline date: does the lookup print current for its located anchor, or resolve it like a source whose baseline is newer than the anchor's confirmation?

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 6 of 19, "Freshness at lookup: revalidation compares the right window and remembers what it checked"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Premise: a section-kept fact prints current for a passage whose baseline is newer than its anchor. Run 2026-10-12 on origin/main with a planted state (anchor verified 2026-01-01 on "thirty", baseline detected 2026-02-01 on "sixty", another section edited since): resolve_source returned outcome verbatim, signal section, so lookup_source prints current: reproduces. The check names the new test by its -k fragment, so the test name carries revalidate_baseline_after_confirmation. Run after BG-geepi6yv: both change resolve and lookup_source. From the SP-tm4wlsve review (ST-mq7we5r2, ST-3zlzfitj), kb/_self/tools.md: a later baseline proves only that nothing changed since. Scenario: anchor verified on thirty, page edited to sixty, detect saved the new baseline with no apply, another section edited later; pack --revalidate finds the fact section equal to the saved baseline and prints current for the stale thirty.
